findings.reason: verify.sh:152 calls JSON.parse with no try/catch. gce_ssh_lastline (line 38-40) pipes only stdout through tail, so stderr from the remote node reaches the workflow log, and Node 22 parse errors quote input near the failure point. Nothing in the repo writes .runtime-openclaw.json, so whether the file holds secrets, and so whether this leaks anything, can't be settled from the code.
findings.claim: If the runtime config is malformed, the uncaught JSON.parse SyntaxError can echo a fragment of the file's raw contents to stderr, and that ends up in the CI log.
findings.evidence: The new line runs `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("/home/node/.openclaw/.runtime-openclaw.json","utf8"))` with no try/catch. In recent Node versions (Check 10 says the container runs Node 22), the SyntaxError from a bad parse quotes the input near the failure point (`Unexpected token 'x', "..." is not valid JSON`). The uncaught exception goes to stderr. `gce_ssh_lastline` captures only stdout (`gce_ssh "$1" | tail -1`), so stderr goes straight into the workflow log. The old `jq -cer ... /home/node/.openclaw/.runtime-openclaw.json` reported only line and column on a parse error. Whether this file holds inline secrets isn't shown in the repo: nothing in the export writes `.runtime-openclaw.json`. The trigger is a corrupt or partly written file at verify time, so this is an unusual path. A fix is to wrap the parse in try/catch, print a fixed message and call `process.exit(1)`.

findings.reason: The other config readers (verify.sh:373 browser probe, deploy.sh:826) use JSON5 and resolve $include, but they read OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, the source config, not .runtime-openclaw.json. Nothing in the repo writes the runtime file, so it can't be shown whether it is strict JSON. The old jq was just as strict, so this is not a regression either way.
findings.claim: Strict JSON.parse rejects the same JSON5/$include input that made jq fail, so the fix may not resolve the failure if the runtime config is JSON5.
findings.evidence: The new probe reads the runtime config with strict `JSON.parse`, so it rejects the same input that made jq fail. jq's `Invalid numeric literal` is what it prints for JSON5-style input such as unquoted keys or comments, and every other config reader in this repo uses `JSON5.parse` and resolves `$include` (browser_probe_js at verify.sh:372-383, deploy.sh:793/826). If `.runtime-openclaw.json` holds JSON5 or `$include` content, `JSON.parse` throws and verify still fails, now with the generic 'Failed to inspect active Google Workspace credential route mode' message. The fix only works if the error came from shell quoting, and nothing in the repo writes this file to show that. Use `JSON5` with `--input-type=module` and resolve includes, as the browser probe does, or first confirm the live file is strict JSON.

findings.reason: Line 152 calls process.exit(1) without printing anything, and line 154 runs jq -r '.mode' on the captured output with no || fail guard under set -euo pipefail (line 2). The line 154 behaviour is unchanged from before this change and only affects diagnostics, so it stays low.
findings.claim: The probe exits 1 with no message when the route is missing, and nothing checks that the output is JSON before the local jq parse at line 154. Operators get a generic failure, or set -e aborts on jq's own error.
findings.evidence: When the probe fails because the route is missing or invalid, it calls `process.exit(1)` without printing anything, and a parse error only shows Node's stack trace on stderr. Either way the operator sees one generic failure message and can't tell 'file not parseable' from 'plugin or route not configured'. Also, the output is never checked to be JSON: if the last SSH line is noise, the local `jq -r '.mode'` at line 154 fails inside an assignment and `set -e` aborts with jq's error instead of a `fail` message, which is how the original incident showed up. Print a reason to stderr before exiting, and add `|| fail` / a `jq -e` check on the local parse.
